title: Mumbai: high volume, weak community activation
recommendation: Do not scale Mumbai acquisition spend on volume alone — fix the incorporation-to-community handoff first, or the extra volume will keep arriving unconverted.
evidence: Mumbai: 780 of 2,021 incorporated founders joined a community (38.6%).
Every other city combined: 71.8% join rate.
Two-proportion test, Holm-corrected across 10 cities: p < 1e-15 (adjusted α = 0.0050).
counterEvidence: This city may have a newer incorporation cohort that simply hasn't had time to onboard into a community yet — re-check this finding after excluding founders incorporated in the last 30 days before reallocating budget.

title: Chennai: strong engagement, weak program conversion — a visibility gap
recommendation: Chennai founders are as active as anywhere else but aren't applying to flagship programs — this reads as a targeting/visibility gap, not weak demand. Push direct program outreach to this city's active cohort before cutting its content budget.
evidence: Chennai: Active rate 77.1% vs. 57.2% pool — at or above the rest of the cohort.
Chennai: 4.8% of active founders applied to a flagship program, vs. 21.0% pool.
Two-proportion test, Holm-corrected across 10 cities: p < 1e-15 (adjusted α = 0.0050).
counterEvidence: A strong Active rate with weak Applied conversion could also mean this city's active founders are genuinely earlier-stage and not yet program-ready — check founder tenure before assuming it's purely a visibility problem.

title: Xport+: small base, disproportionately high application and admit rate
recommendation: Xport+ is only 21% of the active founder base but applies to flagship programs at roughly 2.8x the rate of the rest of the cohort, with a higher admit rate too. This segment reads as underinvested relative to its output — increase content and program-outreach spend aimed at it next quarter.
evidence: Xport+: 38.8% application rate vs. 13.8% pool, on n = 703 active founders.
Xport+ admit/selection rate: 23.4% vs. 9.0% in the rest of the cohort.
Two-proportion test, Holm-corrected across 3 communities: p < 1e-15 (adjusted α = 0.0167).
counterEvidence: A smaller community can swing further on the same underlying noise — the interval above is wider than the larger communities' for exactly that reason. Treat this as a strong lead for next quarter's content plan, not a guaranteed repeat performance.

title: Event RSVPs are the wrong engagement signal — Rize Genie usage predicts applications far better
recommendation: Re-weight the engagement score away from event RSVP count and toward Rize Genie usage frequency. Genie-active founders apply to flagship programs at 2.3x the rate of low-usage founders; high-RSVP founders apply at only 0.9x the rate of low-RSVP founders.

impactRange.label: Lift on program-application rate
impactRange.vsPool: both measured against the same active-founder cohort

evidence: High Genie usage (≥10 sessions/month): 26.9% applied, vs. 11.8% for low usage (p < 1e-15).
High RSVP count (≥5 events): 18.3% applied, vs. 19.6% for low RSVP (p = 3.33e-1).
Genie usage lift (2.28x) exceeds RSVP lift (0.93x) on the same cohort, same outcome definition.
counterEvidence: RSVP count may still matter for a different outcome (e.g. community retention rather than program application) — this finding is scoped specifically to predicting flagship-program applications, not engagement in general.
